reuse.why: The check is written once in assertBankAccountIsNotLinked and used by all five link handlers, though it then wraps it in five provider-named aliases that add nothing.

duplication.why: Five identical one-line alias functions plus five near-identical async registration lambdas repeat the same call shape per provider.

placement.why: The guard is attached in anonymous lambdas at app.method registration instead of inside the link functions (or a shared link step), so a direct call to linkSimpleFinAccount etc. skips it.

scope.why: Only the guard, its wiring and tests are added.

maintainability.why: The rule itself is clean and in one place, but the alias layer and per-handler lambdas mean a new provider needs two more boilerplate pieces and the guard is easy to miss outside registration.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No existing link guard was bypassed; all link handlers call the new shared check.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated pieces are thin, visibly parallel wrappers around one shared check, not reshaped logic.

one_place.where: assertBankAccountIsNotLinked in accounts/app.ts holds the rule (provider + account id, non-deleted, excluding upgradingId); all five link handlers call it.
